chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Hal-Halby, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
You should say in the two prostrations of forgetfulness: 'In the name of Allah and by Allah. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad.'
Al-Halby said, 'And I heard him another time saying: In the name of Allah and by Allah. Peace be upon you, O Prophet, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings.'

key_terms.اللَّهُمَّ صَلِّ: O Allah, send blessings (a specific supplicatory formula)
key_terms.سَجْدَتَيِ السَّهْوِ: The two prostrations performed due to forgetfulness or doubt in prayer

ai.seo_question: What should be recited during the prostrations of forgetfulness in Shia prayer?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the specific dhikr recited during the two prostrations of forgetfulness (sajdat al-sahw), offering two variations: one emphasizing general praise and blessings upon the Prophet and his family, and another directly addressing the Prophet with peace and blessings. The variation reflects the scholarly understanding that sajdat al-sahw serves as a means to rectify minor omissions or distractions in prayer, reinforcing the connection between the worshipper and the Prophet. The second variation, which directly addresses the Prophet, underscores the Shia emphasis on the spiritual presence and intercession of the Ahl al-Bayt during acts of worship.
